body:
ash: noticing a pile of GPU pods pending and CA is just churning out nodes that never come Ready

infra-bot: Alert: autoscaler scaled node-pool/gpu-us-west-2 +5 \u2014 multiple nodes NotReady reported

tori: `kubectl get nodes | egrep gpu` shows several with NotReady,SchedulingDisabled
```
ip-10-2-14-101   NotReady,SchedulingDisabled   0/8     1h
ip-10-2-18-55    NotReady,SchedulingDisabled   0/8     10m
ip-10-2-26-12    NotReady,SchedulingDisabled   0/8     2m
```

eli: grabbing logs from device-plugin + system journal. device-plugin fails to enumerate: `nvidia-smi` exits 1

rachel: device-plugin log snippet:
```
E0615 14:03:02.342 deviceplugin.go:88] failed to list devices: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = nvidia-smi returned exit code 1
stderr: "NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver"
```

ash: checking dmesg on a test node, kernel module load errors:
```
Jun 15 13:59:10 kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
Jun 15 13:59:10 kernel: nvidia: Unknown symbol: nv_alloc_ctl
Jun 15 13:59:11 systemd: nvidia-modprobe.service: Main process exited, code=exited
```

tori: confirmed. AMI v4.2 pushed last night (kernel 5.19.0-40) but AMI's driver package is 520.39 prebuilt for 5.15. ABI mismatch. DKMS not enabled so module not rebuilt at boot.

eli: that explains it. CA sees pending GPU requests, spins up nodes with the bad AMI, they fail the same way -> autoscaler loop + cost.

rachel: immediate mitigation: cordon the gpu-us-west-2 node pool and scale ASG down. keep one diagnostic node for triage.

ops-oncall: doing it now. cordoning pool and setting ASG desired=0, leaving a single diagnostic instance tagged `gpu-diagnostics`.

infra-bot: Action: pool gpu-us-west-2 cordoned by ops-oncall at 14:12 UTC

ash: options for fix: (1) rollback AMI to v4.1 (known-good), (2) enable DKMS driver in AMI or deploy a DKMS builder daemonset, (3) add bootstrap preflight so CA won't accept unhealthy nodes.

tori: rollback is fastest. DKMS/daemonset is safer long-term but costs time. We should also add a preflight script in cloud-init that runs `modinfo nvidia` and `nvidia-smi` and fails init if mismatch. CA will still create the instance but it won't join the cluster if preflight fails (prevents scheduler churn).

eli: opened INFRA-941 to cover rollback + packer integration tests (run `modinfo nvidia`, `nvidia-smi`, and load module). linking the AMI pipeline + packer smoke tests. tagging @tori @rachel.

rachel: also adding an alert: if device-plugin CrashLoop on >=3 nodes in same pool, auto-cordon pool and page infra oncall.

ops-oncall: rolling AMI back to v4.1 now, will spin up two test nodes and validate `nvidia-smi`. ETA ~25m.

ops-oncall: test nodes 2/2 healthy: `nvidia-smi` shows GPUs, device-plugin registered. uncordoning pool and setting ASG desired back to min=2.

eli: watching CA logs and node readiness: new nodes reach Ready, pods schedule to GPUs, no more CA churn.

ash: follow-ups in INFRA-941: add DKMS discussion, implement cloud-init preflight, add CA health gate (require node Ready + `nvidia-smi` ok before marking scale-up complete), and packer smoke tests.

rachel: cost note: autoscaler churn created ~3 hours of wasted spot/ondemand capacity, cost team notified. we'll add a metric for GPU pool churn to alert earlier.

ops-oncall: marking incident mitigated. leaving the alerting changes as high priority.

infra-bot: Thread resolved by ops-oncall at 14:40 UTC
